method: simulated LLM reliability p x D, seeds 0..199
arms: FIXED (trust tail = broken HYBRID) | ADAPT (escalate tail) | CALIB (escalate only when LLM top-picks miscalibrated) | PURE-B (verify all)
verdict: ADAPT fixes the hole (2.00 at all p by escalating the un-verified tail); CALIB makes escalation adaptive but is NOT a free lunch
trilemma: {correctness, autonomy(low escalation), efficiency(low verify)} cannot all be maxed. FIXED sacrifices correctness (silently misses causes). ADAPT sacrifices autonomy (~1 escalation/task) to guarantee correctness. PURE-B sacrifices efficiency (verify all D). CALIB navigates by escalating only when the LLM's top picks verify as non-causal -> escalation rises 0.30->0.58 as reliability falls (real autonomy when the LLM earns trust), but reintroduces a residual miss WORST in the MARGINAL zone (p~0.5 dips below p=0.3): 'looks reliable but isn't' is the danger band.
honest_failure: First CALIB attempt had escal=0.00 everywhere and tracked FIXED -- it read a quick run of confounded decoys at the top as 'reliable', when that run is precisely the LLM being fooled. Corrected signal: trust only when the LLM's MOST-CONFIDENT top picks verify as causal (no decoy ranked above a cause).
design_guidance: The 'trust only verified, C7 overrides' principle is a SPECTRUM set by STAKES: high-risk (R4/R5-like) -> ADAPT or PURE-B (never silently trust); low-risk -> CALIB (calibrated trust at bounded miss risk); FIXED is never acceptable.
honesty_caps: Simulated reliability; the trilemma is the real result, CALIB is a useful-but-imperfect navigator.
